image_prompt: A distinguished German noblewoman in her late fifties to early sixties, the Duchess of Brunswick, captured in austere 1720s aristocratic fashion. She has a commanding, matronly presence with refined, elegant features showing patrician breeding - high cheekbones, a strong nose, and shrewd, discerning eyes that convey both warmth and authority. Her silver-gray hair is styled in the elaborate court fashion of the early 18th century, powdered and arranged in formal curls. She wears an opulent brocade gown in deep burgundy or forest green with intricate gold embroidery, featuring wide panniers, a tightly-laced bodice with elaborate lacework at the neckline and sleeves, and layers of expensive silk. Her costume displays the refined elegance of a wealthy German court - far more ornate than Prussian austerity. Jeweled brooches, pearl necklaces, and rings adorn her person. Her expression is dignified and maternal, with a slight, knowing smile suggesting both worldly sophistication and genuine affection. Her posture is impeccably upright, embodying aristocratic bearing and confidence.
